subject: NovaCorp AWS Marketplace private offer - evidence package & buyer approval flow
messages:
From: Alan Chen <alan.chen@novacorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NovaCorp AWS Marketplace private offer - evidence and buyer approval

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — we liked the latency profiles and the routing options you showed. Procurement asked me to follow up to get the formal evidence pack and to map the approval path for a private offer on AWS Marketplace. Two items in particular:

- Evidence: We need a concise SOC 2 summary, any data residency / KMS statements, and an outline of audit logging we can share with our cloud compliance team. A 1-2 page summary is ideal for their intake.
- Approval flow & term: Our legal team prefers an initial 12-month private offer but Procurement wants flexibility to push to 24 months if pricing is more favorable. We also need to understand who needs to sign on our side (procurement, legal, CFO) depending on ARR/commit.

Can you send the evidence pack and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) that lists the approvals we should expect on both sides and suggested timelines? If possible, include any standard language you require in the marketplace private offer (billing cadence, termination windows, usage true-up).

Target timeline: Procurement would like to get the offer created and in signature routing by the end of March so we can go-live in early April. Is that feasible?

Thanks — attaching our intake form for context (procurement intake referenced but not attached here).

Regards,
Alan Chen
Procurement Manager, NovaCorp
procurement@novacorp.com
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference>
To: Alan Chen <alan.chen@novacorp.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovaCorp AWS Marketplace private offer - evidence and buyer approval

Hi Alan — thanks, glad the demo helped.

Short answer: yes, we can meet your timeline. Below is what we'll provide and the suggested approval sequence we recommend for a smooth private-offer activation.

Evidence pack (we will send as attachments):
- SOC 2 Type II executive summary (2 pages) — control scope, last audit date, auditor contact stub.
- Data residency & encryption note — KMS integration options (customer-managed keys) and supported regions.
- Audit logging & retention outline — what logs are available and typical retention windows.

Private offer term/pricing options:
- Standard options: 12 mo (baseline), 24 mo (discounted 8-12%), 36 mo (custom pricing).
- Billing cadence: monthly usage vs. prepaid commit — both supported; PO can be structured either way.
- Approval gating: we recommend buyer procurement + legal for all POs; CFO/finance approval required if ARR or committed spend > $250k.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Redwood sends evidence pack + draft private-offer terms (today).
2) NovaCorp legal & procurement review (2-4 business days).
3) Pricing/term finalization and CFO sign-off if required (1-5 business days).
4) Seller creates AWS private offer and routes DocuSign to NovaCorp signatories; activation window scheduled upon countersignature.

Attachments included: procurement-MAP.xlsx (MAP + owner matrix) and nova-soc2-summary.pdf (executive summary).

If you prefer a 12-month term for now with an explicit renewal option to extend to 24 months at a pre-agreed tiered discount, we can bake that into the private-offer metadata so the buyer has the renewal option without having to re-negotiate pricing.

Questions for you:
- What is your expected first-year commit or estimated monthly spend? (This helps us advise discount tiers.)
- Who should be the primary signatory on your side for procurement & legal?

We can also loop in our PS lead to draft a quick PSA onboarding outline so there's no delay post-activation.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>
To: Alan Chen <alan.chen@novacorp.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2025 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovaCorp AWS Marketplace private offer - evidence and buyer approval

Thanks for the context Alan — copying a couple folks internally who will own activation and onboarding.

Quick clarifications on approvals and next steps:
- For private offers on AWS we typically record the following approvers on the offer metadata: procurement contact, legal signatory, and finance approver if the initial committed value exceeds $250k. If NovaCorp expects to keep billing monthly usage with a nominal commit, the CFO step often isn’t required.
- Term structure: Irene's suggestion of a 12-month term with an optional auto-renew to 24 months at a negotiated discount is our preferred approach for pilot-to-scale customers. It reduces procurement friction while keeping you protected.
- PSA/onboarding: attaching a short PSA outline so your technical onboarding team knows the pre-activation checklist (names, IAM roles, expected traffic pattern, go-live smoke tests).

Action items for NovaCorp (requested):
1) Confirm preferred term (12 vs 24) and whether you want prepaid commit or monthly usage billing.
2) Share procurement & legal signatory names and emails for DocuSign routing.
3) Quick estimate of expected monthly tokens/usage so we can advise optimal instance sizing in the private offer.

Irene / Jonas — once Alan confirms we will draft the private-offer proposal and generate a DocuSign envelope.

We talked it over internally. Decision: we will go with a 12-month private offer (pilot) with a contractual option to extend to 24 months at a pre-agreed discount tier if we hit the target usage in Q4. Procurement will route legal and procurement signatories first; CFO approval is not required for the initial pilot level (~$120k estimated first year), so that should keep the path faster.

Requested next steps from Redwood:
- Please create the AWS private offer with the 12-month term and the renewal option flag.
- Route DocuSign to the following signatories:
  - Procurement: Alan Chen <alan.chen@novacorp.com>
  - Legal: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@novacorp.com>
- Share the HubSpot deal link once created and the DocuSign envelope ID.
- Target activation: 2025-04-01 if countersignature completed by 2025-03-28.
